chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ibn al-Barqi, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Ten places in which one does not pray: clay, water, the bathhouse, graves, the main roads, anthills, camel enclosures, flowing water, marshland, and snow.

key_terms.الطِّينُ: Clay or mud, often considered impure or distinct from standard prayer surfaces.
key_terms.الْحَمَّامُ: The bathhouse or public bath, a place of ritual impurity.
key_terms.الْقُبُورُ: Graves, where prayer is often performed but with specific rulings on validity or preference.
key_terms.مَسَانُّ الطَّرِيقِ: Main roads or thoroughfares, places of public transit.
key_terms.مَعَاطِنُ الْإِبِلِ: Camel enclosures or resting places for camels.

ai.seo_question: What are the ten places where prayer is not performed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines ten specific surfaces or locations where prayer is disliked (makruh) or invalid, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on purity (taharah) and avoiding impure or distracting environments. The list ranges from natural elements like clay, water, and snow to specific places such as bathhouses, graves, and camel enclosures, highlighting the importance of the physical context of worship. This enumeration serves as a practical guide for believers to ensure their prayers are performed on clean, distinct, and respectful surfaces.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Ibn Al Barqy, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Fazl, from the one who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Ten places one cannot pray therein – The clay, and the water, and the bathroom (bathhouse), and the graves, and the main road, and the anthill, and enclosure of the camels, and flowing of the water, and the marshland, and the snow’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah has narrated from ibn al-Barqiy from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl from those who narrated to him has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Salah (prayer) is not performed in ten places, such as in clay, water, bath houses, on graves, on main roads, ant’s colonies, camel’s barns, water beds, salt grounds and on snow.’”
